# results/ : what each file is (generated by `scripts/06_tables.py`, `09_predictive.py`, `10_tables_more.py`)

**Status: provisional until the core batch is finished** (`datasets_computed.csv` lists the data sets present; `n_boot` in each row says the bootstrap size used, 500 = final, smaller = a test run that the batch will overwrite). All rows are real data (`synthetic=0`) unless a file says otherwise.

Common definitions (details in `PREANALYSIS.md`): conclusion = ordered model pair (a above b) in the BT-MLE leaderboard (pair-aggregated counts, ties as half a win, ridge 1e-4). `k_upper` = smallest number of altered comparisons found by search whose exact refit puts b at or above a (a verified upper bound on the minimum; `k_lower` only where an exact/LP anchor exists). `perturbation` = `delete` (remove comparisons) or `flip` (change outcomes, non-dominated types). `z` = gap / bootstrap SE (cluster bootstrap by battle / question / game, B in `n_boot`), `z_fisher` = gap / model-based SE. `F = k_upper * g_max / SE_boot`, `Q = F / z_boot`. `Q_null`, `k_null_*` = same-graph parametric-bootstrap replicates (same pairs and counts, fitted scores, tie rate; 20 replicates) at the pair's `z_fisher`. `k_null_pred = Q_null * gap / g_max` is the k* the null predicts for this very pair without searching on the real data; `k_upper / k_null_pred = Q / Q_null`.

| file | one row per | note |
|---|---|---|
| `datasets.csv`, `datasets_computed.csv` | data set | N, models, density, tie rate, cluster unit, data version and sha256 |
| `fragility_conclusions.csv` | data set x conclusion x perturbation | 60 pairs spread over z (+ all top-1 pairs) per data set and family; `Q_null*`, `k_null*` as above |
| `fragility_by_z.csv` | data set x perturbation x z stratum ([0,1),[1,2),[2,4),[4,8),[8,inf) on `z_fisher`) | `k_med`, null: `k_null_med` (replicate pairs in the stratum), `k_null_pred_med`, `k_ratio_*` (median of k*/null-predicted k*, bootstrap over pairs) |
| `top1_conclusions.csv` | data set x perturbation | top-1 vs top-2, and the cheapest rival for the top-1 |
| `real_minus_null.csv` | data set x perturbation | Delta = mean over pairs with `z_fisher` in [1,8] of log Q - log Q_null, jackknife over models (C1, C4) |
| `matched_contrasts.csv` | contrast x member x perturbation | joint cluster bootstrap on identical battles/questions (`07_matched.py`); `paired_*` = difference to the reference member; equivalence margin 0.15 on log Q |
| `survival_curves.csv` | data set x perturbation x separation definition x subset x curve x budget | `curve`: adversarial (fraction of separated pairs with k* above the budget) or random_delete / random_flip (1 - P_flip of random alteration of the same size, interpolated from the f-grid of `02_random.py`). Every row carries the budget in four units (`b_count`, `b_se`, `b_sqrtN`, `b_frac`); `axis` says which unit the grid is regular in. `sep_def`: published (non-overlapping 95% percentile model CIs, B=500) or gap (CI of the pair's gap excludes 0). `subset`: separated, separated_top10, separated_z1_8. Wilson intervals treating pairs as independent (a narrow, optimistic interval) |
| `predictive_rule.csv`, `predictive_rule_units.csv` | term / held-out fold | WLS of log k* on log z, log N, log density, tie rate; leave-one-dataset-out and leave-one-design-out |

shown.message:
The Discussion and Limitations section is now written and pushed to `dev`. I haven't checked the build on `dev`, and the paper is still not ready to offer as a version.

**Done this turn**
- The Discussion section now has the limitations text: what the data cannot say (design is confounded with dataset), where the measurement applies (the density, tie-rate and size ranges the real data cover), and the scope of the estimator and threat model. These paragraphs state no new numbers.
- The "what the results mean" and "practice" paragraphs are placeholders for now. They get written from the final results.
- I added the `sec:experiments` label to the Experiments stub so the Discussion's cross-reference resolves.
- I worded the claim about the search versus the exact optimum as a comparison, not a result, because I haven't seen those numbers yet.
- `figtab-repo` has answered my request in `figtab-repo`#4 and #3. Table 2 is now a main-text subset (largest dataset per design) with per-family appendix tables, and the margin is 0.15.

**Still blocking the rest of the paper**
- **Missing outputs:** `experiment-repo` is still running. `results/` has no `matched_contrasts.csv` yet, and the search-at-scale and subsampling results are not there either.
- **Provisional rows:** `mtbench_gpt4` still has only 20 bootstrap resamples, below the final 500.
- **What I'm holding back:** the abstract, introduction, experiments section and checklist, because they depend on those outputs.

**Next:** once those outputs are final I'll write the experiments section, introduction, abstract and checklist, then offer a `release` version. I'll take every number in the text from `results/` by script and ask `experiment-repo` to confirm what each one is.
